FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standarc^s on 27 April 1989, after the 
draft finalized by the Small Tools Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical 
Engineering Division Council. 

This standard has been prepared based on prevalent practices in Indian industry and developments 
at international level. In the preparation of this standard, considerable assistance has been derived 
from: 

DIN 8375 : 1981 Subland twist drill with morse taper shank for clearance holes and counter- 
sinks for countersunk head screw 

Other Indian Standards on subland drills are: 

IS 12687 : 1989 Small tools — Subland twist drills with morse taper shank for countersunk 
holes prior to tapping screw threads — Specification 

IS 12689: 1989 Small tools — Subland drills with parallel shank for clearance holes and 
counterbores for slotted cheese head screws — Specification 

IS 12690: 1989 Small tools — Subland twist drills with morse taper shank for clearance 
holes and counterbores for slotted cheese head metric screw — Specifica- 
tion 

IS 12691 : 1989 Small tools — Subland twist drills with parallel shank for holes prior to 
tapping screw threads — Specification 

IS 12692: 1989 Small tools —• Subland twist drills with parallel shank for clearance holes 
and countersink for countersunk head screws — Specification

SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

!•! This standard covers dimensions and other 
requirements for the subland twist drills with 
morse taper shank for producing clearance holes 
and countersinks for countersunk head screws 
M5 to M14 conforming to IS 3406 (Part I ) : 
1986 'Dimensions for countersinks and counter- 
bores: Part I Countersinks ( second revision )'. 



2 REFERENCES

tions and counterbores : 
Part 1 Countersinks 
( second revision )

7778 : 1975 
10915 : 1984

For the purpose of this standard, the definitions 
given in IS 10915 : 1984 shall apply.

4.2 Tolerances 

Tolerance on the flute length /^ and overall length 
/ shall be ± 5 mm. 

5 MATERIAL 

Material of subland twist drill shall be as given 
in IS 5099 : 1983. 

6 HARDNESS 

Hardness of subland twist drills shall be as given 
in IS 5099 : 1983. 

7 GENERAL REQjUIREMENTS 

7.1 Tool Type N, right-hand cutting will be 
supplied, unless otherwise specified. 

7.2 The diameter d and di shall be measured as 
near to the point as practicable. 

7.3 While using this drill, cutting speed 
should be selected according to the large dia- 
meter 'd* and the feed rate according to small 
( pilot ) diameter *di\ 

7.4 For requirements not covered in this stan- 
dard; it shall conform to the requirements as 
given in IS 5099 : 1983. 

8 PROTECTIVE COATINGS 

Subland twist drills shall be given protective 
coating as given in IS 5099 : 1983. 



9 SAMPLING 

The sampling and the criteria of acceptance shall 
be in accordance with IS 7778 : 1975. 

10 TESTS 

Subland twist drills shall be tested according to 
IS 5099: 1983. 

11 DESIGNATION 

11.1 A subland twist drill with more taper shank 
having diameter rf= 13 mm and step diameter 
di = 6*6 mm Tool Type N, for right-hand cutting 
made from high speed steel and conforming to 
this standard shall be designated as: 

Subland Twist Drill 13 x 6*6 IS 12688 

11.2 When required with tool type other than 
N, H or S should be added in the designation 
after the diameter as appropriate. 

12 MARKING 

Subland twist drills shall be marked as given in 
IS 5099 : 1983. 

13 PACKING AND PACKAGING 

13.1 Subland twist drills shall be packed as 
given in IS 5099 : 1983. 



StancUrd Mark 

The use of the Standard N^ark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the pro- 
ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that 
standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
of the Standard Mark niay be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian StondafSs AcL li^6 ib pt6moi^ 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of 
goods and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in 
any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in 
the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or 
grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications). BIS. 

Revision of Indian Standards

are issued from time to time. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession
